title: Week Summary: Information and Concurrency Viewpoints

concepts.name: Information viewpoint
concepts.description: A viewpoint focused on data concepts, ownership, lifecycle, integrity, and movement across the system.

concepts.name: Data ownership
concepts.description: The architectural assignment of authority for creating, changing, validating, and interpreting data.

concepts.name: Canonical information model
concepts.description: A shared representation of important domain information used to align systems or integrations.

concepts.name: Data lifecycle
concepts.description: The stages through which data is created, used, retained, archived, deleted, or audited.

concepts.name: Concurrency viewpoint
concepts.description: A viewpoint focused on independently executing elements and their coordination.

concepts.name: Concurrent element
concepts.description: A process, thread, task, worker, or active runtime unit that can execute independently.

concepts.name: Synchronization mechanism
concepts.description: A technique such as locking, messaging, transactions, or coordination protocol used to manage concurrent behavior.

concepts.name: Back pressure
concepts.description: A control mechanism that prevents upstream work from overwhelming downstream capacity.

concepts.name: Data consistency
concepts.description: The degree to which data remains correct and aligned across operations, stores, and system boundaries.

concepts.name: Eventual consistency
concepts.description: A consistency model where replicas or dependent systems converge after a delay rather than immediately.

concepts.name: Idempotency
concepts.description: The property that repeating an operation has the same effect as performing it once.

concepts.name: Compensating action
concepts.description: A corrective operation used to undo or offset effects when a distributed workflow cannot use a single transaction.
